reason: Drizzle Kit legacy loader uses transform, not the vulnerable esbuild development server. No esbuild serve endpoint is exposed. Upstream loader replacement requires a separate compatibility check; a cross-major override is not applied.

Xcode project tooling uses random UUIDs for local project identifiers, not authorization or untrusted buffer writes. The installed CLI retains uuid 7 through xcode; forcing uuid 11 changes the dependency contract. Recheck upstream xcode support before mobile distribution.

The exact 4.3.1 installation is locally fixed by patches/deepmerge@4.3.1.patch in index.js and the CJS/UMD distributions; writes of __proto__ from both target and source use own data properties. check:dependency-audit first verifies the patch registration and actual research dependency resolutions against poisoning regressions, including ESM consumption. Registry audit still reports the unchanged 4.3.1 version. This review covers only these three research paths and must be removed when an upstream fix is adopted.

The existing v10 API is retained. check-minimatch-patches.test.mjs verifies the exact registered patch and installed CJS/ESM consumer paths, including the unbundled glob consumers, bounded amplification and ordinary matching before the audit. Registry still reports the original version; replace this local fix and remove these exact paths when a compatible upstream update is adopted.

GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 describes firstPhasePreProcess globparts amplification at optimizationLevel >= 2. This exact legacy major has neither preprocessing phase nor optimizationLevel (introduced in v7); its callable CommonJS API cannot be replaced with v11 without migrating consumers. check-minimatch-patches.test.mjs verifies every reviewed installed path lacks that implementation and exercises matching through the legacy API. This is an applicability review for this advisory only, not a general ReDoS exemption; reassess these paths by expiry.
